result.title: Multimodal Masked Diffusion Autoencoder for Modeling Impaired Driving
result.comment: Equal contribution: John Gideon and Anshul Gupta. 8 pages, 6 figures. Submitted to CVPR 2027
result.summary: Human cognitive state (e.g., distraction, stress), gaze, and behavior interact with the driving environment in subtle ways that AI could use to assist drivers, but ground-truth labels for human cognitive state levels are costly to obtain at scale. We propose a multimodal masked-diffusion autoencoder, ID-MAE, that adds a self-supervised objective to impairment prediction: alongside predicting the impairment label as a masked token, it reconstructs masked gaze and trajectory. To probe the effects of different modalities and types of impairments on model inference, we introduce DIVERT, a driving-simulator dataset containing 103 hours of driving data (n = 109) with ten impairment inductions spanning cognitive, visual, and emotional states, recorded with gaze, vehicle state, and scene video. We demonstrate how ID-MAE affords significant improvements in impairment inference results on both the DIVERT dataset and existing datasets, and enables strong results in additional tasks, such as trajectory and gaze prediction. For location-matched pairs, our model achieves a paired AUC of 0.706 for impairment detection on DIVERT, compared to 0.590 without reconstruction loss, improving over existing baselines. We probe the design space in terms of input modalities, masking scheme, positional encoding, attention mechanism, and decoding. We also investigate the interaction between various impairments in training and inference, demonstrating that visually demanding distractions are separable from cognitive distractions. Code and data will be available upon acceptance.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 ID-MAE：一种多模态掩码扩散自编码器，在把受损标签作为掩码 token 预测的同时，自监督重建被掩码的注视与轨迹，并发布 DIVERT 驾驶模拟数据集，探查输入模态、掩码方案、位置编码、注意力与解码方式的设计空间。
AI.relevance_reason: 掩码扩散解码与多模态掩码重建目标，可能为 LVR 中并行/扩散式 latent 状态生成及重建监督的贡献分配提供可核查线索；但任务本身是驾驶受损推断，与视觉推理主线距离较远。
